git grep -i -E "revok|denylist|blacklist|logout|signout" stage-1 over *.cs and *.dart: no match. AuthController has only the login action.

RFC 6265: "The semantics of the cookie-value are not defined by this document." and "servers that wish to store arbitrary data in a cookie-value SHOULD encode that data". Lesson: a cookie "can carry a session id or a whole token"; the transport does not decide the model.

app-state.md: "The in-memory cache provider stores session data in the memory of the server where the app resides. In a server farm scenario: Use sticky sessions ... A better approach is to use a Redis, SQL Server, or Azure Postgres distributed cache". distributed.md lists "Survives server restarts" as a benefit of a distributed cache, i.e. in-memory does not.

Validation parameters in Program.cs check issuer, audience, signing key and lifetime only; nothing stored is consulted, so no per-token ending is possible without adding server-side state. Lesson wording ("needs something extra on the server") is conditional and matches.

app-state.md: "Session data is deleted either when the ISession.Clear implementation is called or when the session expires." A request carrying the old id then finds no data. Lesson states it for the general model, consistent with the doc.
Kind opinion with its condition stated in the sentence ("When ending a login immediately matters more than avoiding a store"); follows from claims 9 and 10.

Docs: "The client that requests the JWT can request data from an API resource by using the Authorization header and a bearer token." Lesson only says "`Bearer` just labels what follows as a token" - no stronger than the doc.

issues.text: The last sentence of How it works carries three steps (nothing to delete, ending early needs a store, that store is what tokens avoid) with a dash aside in the middle. I read it twice to see the 'which' refers to the list of ended tokens.
issues.quote: ending one token before it expires needs something extra on the server — such as a list of ended tokens to check each request against — which is the kind of store tokens were meant to avoid.
issues.fix: Split after 'check each request against': end that sentence there, then add 'That list is itself a store — the kind tokens were meant to avoid.'

issues.text: The correct option restates the lesson's sentence 'this app has no code that can end one earlier' almost word for word, so I could pick it by recognition rather than reasoning about the missing store.
issues.quote: No code in this app can stop just this one token; it stays valid for about seven more hours.
issues.fix: Reword option a around the reason, e.g. 'The server kept nothing about this token to delete, so it keeps working until about seven hours from now.'
